original_context: Group theory: homomorphism f:A→B of abelian groups respecting addition, f(a+a')=f(a)+f(a'), necessarily preserving additive identities and inverses.
definition: For groups (A,+) and (B,+) written additively, a group homomorphism f:A→B is a function satisfying f(a+a′)=f(a)+f(a′) for every a,a′∈A. Consequently f(0_A)=0_B and f(−a)=−f(a).
reasoning: The independent screened kernel-of-abelian-group-homomorphism definition uses an additive homomorphism as an input; it is not a standalone definition of the map. An additive group homomorphism imposes operation preservation but not module scalar-linearity, ring multiplication preservation, or injectivity.

sources.section: Group Homomorphism, operation preservation and identity/inverse properties
sources.relevance: Directly checked group-operation preservation and deductions for identities and inverses; this candidate specializes general notation to groups written additively.

comparison.rationale: Reviewed all 595 independent screened and 16 provisional meanings for general homomorphisms, linear maps and additive groups. The corpus has group-homomorphism uses but no standalone exact meaning giving only additive group-operation preservation; no module or ring linearity is implied. Earlier staged items are topology, relation, matrix and graph meanings, not homomorphisms. All 14 previously staged preliminary dispositions were also considered; none is an exact whole-meaning duplicate of this candidate.

mathematical_assumptions: A and B are groups expressed with additive operation, not necessarily abelian unless an application states so.
Identity and inverses are consequences, not independent optional axioms.
No preservation of scalar multiplication is assumed.
